title: Bridge a remote control to interchangeable devices
description: A RemoteControl abstraction provides togglePower() and setVolume(int) to the user. It holds a reference to a Device implementation (TV or Radio) and delegates all state changes to it. An AdvancedRemote extends RemoteControl with a mute() shortcut. Wire up the bridge so remotes and devices can be combined freely without subclassing every combination.
hints: Device is an interface — TV and Radio are provided for you
RemoteControl stores a Device and delegates togglePower() and setVolume() to it
AdvancedRemote extends RemoteControl and adds mute() by calling setVolume(0)
issues: Without a bridge, every remote-device combination needs its own subclass (TVRemote, RadioRemote, AdvancedTVRemote, …)
Adding a new device type forces changes to the remote hierarchy and vice versa
overallGoal: Use the Bridge pattern to let RemoteControl and Device vary independently, so any remote can control any device with no extra subclasses.
goals: Define a Device interface with power(), volumeUp(), volumeDown(), and setVolume() methods
Have RemoteControl hold a Device reference and delegate all power and volume calls to it
Implement AdvancedRemote.mute() by calling setVolume(0) on the device
